match: is not a column type this library renders
why: A type is the one part of a statement the renderer does not quote: it writes the layout's spelling as it is (schema/002). Until 20 November 2026 this layout rendered CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "order" ("id" uuid, "x" int); DROP TABLE "victim"; CREATE TABLE "z" ("y" int, ...), and PostgreSQL runs several statements in one simple query. A signed map is ours, and the threat model promises that even one from a compromised control plane cannot make the client's provisioning run SQL of its choosing. So every type is read first by one grammar: words of the two vocabularies, ASCII digits, spaces, zones in single quotes, parentheses at most four deep and commas only inside them.
